THE INSCRIPTION OF THE WEST BOHEMIAN SPA TRIANGLE ON UNESCO
WORLD HERITAGE LIST WITHIN THE GSE SERIAL NOMINATION
by Vladimír Kajlik
(Mariánské Lázně Site manager for UNESCO)
Abstract
The Great Spas of Europe (GSE), as an integral unit of European spas heritage providing
exceptional testimony to the phenomenon of European spas of the 19th century, is a
multinational property of serial nomination seeking entry to the UNESCO World Heritage
List (WHL). This serial property of 11 leading European spa towns of the GSE project
consists of: Baden bei Wien, Bad Ems, Baden Baden, Bad Kissingen, City of Bath,
Františkovy Lázně, Karlovy Vary, Mariánské Lázně, Montecatini Terme, City of Spa,
and Vichy. These spa sites, i.e. components of the GSE, are positioned in seven European
countries: Austria, Belgium, the Czech Republic, France, Germany, Italy, and the United
Kingdom.
The article summarizes the procedure and steps taken by the Member States of the World
Heritage Convention (WHC) when seeking the nomination of properties on their territory to
be accepted for the inscription to the World Heritage List. The procedural steps of the serial
nomination and the selection criteria for the designated property to be inscribed are provided
on the case of the serial nomination of the GSE, initiated by the Czech Republic in 2011,
which is now in its closing phase.
Keywords: World Heritage List, UNESCO WHL, The Great Spas of Europe (GSE), Outstanding
Universal Value (OUV), OUV Criteria, International Council for Monuments and Settlements
(ICOMOS), World Heritage Committee (WHC), Operational Guidelines for the Implementation of the
World Heritage Convention (OG IWHC), The West Bohemian Spa Triangle (WBST), Františkovy
Lázně, Karlovy Vary, Mariánské Lázně.

************
Introduction
The aforementioned States (contracting States Parties), in submitting their proposal for the
serial nomination of so-called tangible properties on their territories, after careful
consideration and thoughtful deliberation, have decided to seek their nomination to the World
Heritage List. By creating the conditions for the rise of a legal entity The Great Spas of
Europe (GSE) on the soil of the Czech Republic, the GSE entity is pursuing entry into the
UNESCO World Heritage List.
Technically speaking neither Mariánské Lázně nor the West Bohemian Spa Triangle (WSBT),
are seeking this nomination to the World Heritage List on their own, individually, but rather,
it is The Great Spas of Europe components as one legal entity of seven European countries,
consisting of 11 famous European spa towns, whose cultural and historical framework
defines the group’s initiative for serial nomination that can be graphically denoted as follows:

1

 Figure 1: Cultural historical framework of the GSE. Source: Author

The Great Spas of Europe (GSE) phenomenon is a collective expression of social
interactions across centuries in shared common geography, and as such embodies the
essential instruments through which human beings constitute and articulate their collective
European heritage and cultural aspirations by means of their common history.
1 The WBST Procedure to the UNESCO WHL Inscription
Only countries which have signed the World Heritage Convention and are committed to
protecting their natural and cultural heritage may submit proposals for the nomination of
properties on their territory wishing to be included and inscribed on the UNESCO World
Heritage List. The idea to nominate the well-known West Bohemian Spa Triangle,
Františkovy Lázně, Karlovy Vary, Marianské Lázně, for inscription on the WH List originated
from the Czech Republic in Karlovy Vary by the end of 2010. The project gained clearer
contours during the international meeting of experts convening the next year in Karlovy Vary
and after considering the architectural, cultural and social values of the three spa sites
recommending a joint statement. Declaration or the Karlovy Vary Memorandum as it was
named, was issued during the negotiations by the negotiating states parties on May 19-21
2011. The Karlovy Vary summit outlined a plan and strategy on how to achieve a specific
joint objective, including spelling out criteria for UNESCO international serial nomination.
The initiative of the proceedings was undertaken under the auspices of the former Mayor of
Karlovy Vary Petr Kulhánek.
1.1 Provisional inventory (TL)
The first step in the process was to create a Tentative List (TL) of important natural and
cultural monuments located within the defined areas of the GSE. In case of the Czech
Republic: the WBST consisting of Františkovy Lázně, Karlovy Vary and Mariánské Lázně.
The work on the preparation of the nomination dossier began in 2011, when the group of
main stakeholders the management group of convening Mayors, The Mayors Steering Group
(MSG), has been created by the participants. This TL inventory is called provisional because
it provides a forecast of the properties characteristics under consideration which the
contracting States Parties have decided to submit for registration as a set of spa properties
which could and would be initially updated on a regular basis. This is an important step
because the World Heritage Committee cannot consider a nomination for the World Heritage
List of any properties without being included on the list of the WH monuments of any
particular country concerned applying for the inscription in advance.
2

 1.2 Nomination Dossier (ND)
During the process and creation of this provisional or Tentative list, in cooperation of the
parties involved, the WBST has been selected, and the step enabled to start planning when
and how to submit the nomination documentation of Spa sites for the WHL inscription. In
general, The World Heritage Centre shall offer advice and assistance to contracting States
Parties in the preparation of their inventory, which shall be as complete as possible and shall
provide for the inclusion of all necessary documentation, including maps. Thus prepared
documentation, i.e. Nomination dossier is submitted to the World Heritage Centre for review
and for checking whether it is complete. After the nomination dossier is completed, it is
delivered to the relevant Advisory Bodies (AB) for further evaluation.
1.3 Advisory Bodies (AB)
Each nominated property is evaluated independently by two Advisory Bodies (AB) mandated
by the World Heritage Convention (WHC): these bodies are the International Council for
Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS), and the International Union for Conservation of Nature
(IUCN), which provide the World Heritage Committee with their assessments of nominated
cultural monuments and natural sites. The third advisory body is the International Centre for
the Study of the Conservation and Restoration of Cultural Properties (ICCROM), an intergovernmental organisation that provides expert advice to the committees on the protection of
cultural monuments and educational activities.
1.4 The World Heritage Committee (WHC)
Once the selected properties (sites) have been nominated and evaluated, it is up to the Intergovernmental Committee on World Heritage (IGC WH) to make a final decision on its
registration. This committee meets once a year to decide which monuments will be included
on the World Heritage List. The World Heritage Committee may also postpone its decision
(deference) and request further information from the contracting Parties (State Parties) on the
nominated properties (in our case, the proposed components of the WBST Františkovy Lázně,
Karlovy Vary and Mariánské Lázně).

Chart 1: Steps of the Nomination Process. Source: Baird, Melissa F.:UNESCO's WHL Process

1.5 The Referral of the ND for Inscription on the UNESCO WHL.
On January 22, 2019, the submitted Nomination dossier of the Great Spa of Europe (GSE) on
the UNESCO WHL has been officially signed by 11 Mayors of the GSE spa towns at a joint
WHC meeting in Paris.
3

 Figure 2: Signatures of 11 Mayors of the GSE serial nomination at the submitting Nominations ceremony
in Paris, on January 22, 2019

For the West Bohemian Spa Triangle the admission protocol has been signed by: Mayor Jan
Kuchař for Františkovy Lázně, Mayor of Karlovy Vary Andrea Pfefffer Ferklová for Karlovy
Vary, and Mayor Martin Kalina for Mariánské Lázně.

2 Values and criteria for the selection to the UNESCO WHL nomination
In general, to be included on the World Heritage List, the nominated property must
demonstrate so-called outstanding universal value (OUV) and meet at least one of the ten
selection criteria. These criteria are explained in the Operational Guidelines for the
Implementation of the World Heritage Convention (OG IWHC). In addition to the text of the
World Heritage Convention, these Guidelines are the main working instruments in the field of
World Heritage. Their criteria are regularly revised by the World Heritage Committee to
reflect the evolution of the World Heritage concept itself.
2.1 Attributes and definitions of the OUV for nominated properties of the GSE
Outstanding universal value is a technical collocation officially translated into Czech as
Vyjímečná světová hodnota and is commonly referred to in Czech texts by the English
initialism OUV. It is a key element clearly and distinctly defined within the framework of the
system for protection and management of the nominated properties (Spa sites) on the
UNESCO World Heritage List, which consists of the main elements, or so-called principal
elements, listed below, in point 2.3.

2.2 Values and selection of criteria for nominated properties to the WHL in general.
To the end of 2004, the World Heritage Sites (WHS) used to be selected on the basis of six
cultural and four natural criteria. By adopting the revised Operational Guidelines (OG for
IWHC) in 2005, and since 2005, there has been only one set of ten (10) criteria which must be
adhered to. On the basis of these criteria and the justification (authentication) of the
uniqueness of the outstanding universal value of the nominated property and the evaluation of
the criteria of the nominated property by international experts of ICOMOS, the final Report to
the World Heritage Committee for a decision is drawn up and submitted.

6

 2.4 The West Bohemian Spas represent their OUV through above criteria
Mariánské Lázně embodies in its LMP 61 principal elements, which are an integral part of the
historically defined period (1700-1930s). The selected criteria for the OUV of the spa town
are criteria ii and iii of the World Heritage as basic or main elements for the use of natural and
climatic resources in the therapeutic landscape and its surroundings, and criteria iv and vi as
auxiliary, supporting elements amplifying integrity and authenticity, i.e. the originality of the
most dominant key elements for the component of the nominated property.
2.5 Administration and Protection of authenticity and integrity of the Properties
Protection and preservation are important, if not key aspects that we must bear in mind in the
overall management of nominated properties: Since 1992, significant interaction between
people and the natural environment have been recognised as cultural landscapes, in the
context of The Great Spas of Europe we have had begun talking about the cultural and
therapeutic landscapes.
3. ICOMOS Evaluation Mission (EM) in The West Bohemian Spas
The evaluation mission of ICOMOS in the framework of the GSE evaluation process took
place in three spa locations of the Karlovy Vary region – Františkovy Lázně, Karlovy Vary,
Mariánské Lázně – in autumn 2019. On Friday, September 27 2019, the EM team arrived
from Vienna to Františkovy Lázně. The format of the evaluation was based on inspections of
spa sites accompanied by designated team of ICOMOS experts. At the end of each tour,
aggregated discussions took place in the form of questions and answers. On September 29, the
mission arrived to Mariánské Lázně. After completing its mission in ML, on September 30,
afternoon, the EM team departed to Karlovy Vary. The conclusion of the ICOMOS mission
has been announced via the closing Press conference during the summit in Karlovy Vary with
the official publication of the Press release on the nomination of The Great Spas of Europe
with all representatives from the participating seven states present. The KV conference
introduced international experts, politicians, mayors, site managersof individual spa towns,
and other participants involved in this serial nomination project. After the Press conference,
the EM ICOMOS members flew back to Paris. The GSE ICOMOS Interim Report Summary
has been published in December 2019 with additional inquiries requests containing
requirements to provide some additional information arising from the Evaluation Mission in
The West Bohemian Spas.
3.1 Summary of the ICOMOS World Heritage Panel meeting in Paris
The ICOMOS Evaluation Mission submitted its assessments to the World Heritage Panel by
the end of November (11/21/2019). The assessment document is 80 pages plus long. The
appraisal of the results of the Evaluation Mission has been carried out. The questions from
November 2019 were answered. These were followed up by further inquiries, such as the
questions related to the division of protection zones within individual nominated properties,
the definitions of the 'specific protection zones', i.e. buffer zones of the urban conservation
areas etc.
3.2 Interim ICOMOS Report from the WHC
The GSE ICOMOS Interim Report requested new questions to which answers were prepared
and delivered to the WH Committee in January 2020. More responses could follow when the
World Heritage Committee meets in July 2020, in China. The decision to travel to China was
due to be resolved by May 2020. It was supposed to be the first trans-national serial
nomination of its kind ever. The full representation of participants was expected to be in place
for the nomination ceremony planned in Fuzhou (Foochow), southeastern Fujian Province.
7

 3.3 The Schedule of the WHC meeting in China, summer 2020
The Chinese meeting of the WHC was planned in Fuzhou, southeastern Fujian Province, in
summer 2020. The following two weeks, from June 26 to July 9, were due for the WHC
meeting in China. The nomination was then considered sometime from late July to the first
week of August. Exact details of the arrangement have not been released. If the nomination in
China proceeded well, all 11 spa towns representatives of the GSE serial nomination were
expected to participate. The State Parties were definitely ready to display a strong delegations
in joining. It was assumed that at least one expert from each European spa town should have
been present alongside with representativesn of their spa towns.

3.4. After the COVID-19 outbreak problems in 2020 and beyond
Following the release of ICOMOS' Interim Report, there has been a crisis caused by the
circumstances surrounding the global COVID-19 pandemic. As the result of the global
COVID-19 crisis, the July 2020 meeting in China has been cancelled. The new date of the
WHC meeting was renegotiated and the event moved toward the end of June, beginning of
July, 2021. The WHC meeting in China has been therefore rescheduled to June/July 2021.
From the pressure under the new circumstances and due to global restrictions and various
emergency measures undertaken by the State Parties from February to December 2020, all
planned actions of the WHC nomination process have been halted or suspended until further
notice. All ensuing international, regional, even municipal meetings, proceedings or
communications from April 2020 were conducted online, in the form of video conferences,
via zoom calls or other communication channels.
The restricted regime of states not only persists until the end of December 2020, but in many
cases it can be anticipated beyond through 2021 due to the expected prolongations of
restrictive measures especially in the areas of international tourism and hospitality businesses
until the first half of 2021 in different parts of the world and maybe beyond.

3.5 Potential recommendations of ICOMOS
The minutes with conclusions from the evaluation mission of the WHC panel were issued in
February 2020. The concept of a serial GSE nomination has been recognized. If challenged,
it would cause a problem internationally. Currently, various legislations of participating
countries and the issues of their possible coordination are being addressed and proposed.
Issues such as joint marketing and communication planning strategies of participants in the
GSE serial nomination framework are also addressed. Activities od the GSE are being
reoriented to the Marketing and Torusim fields under the emergency regimes of the states.
3.6 Scenarios planning – WHC ICOMOS decision by the end of 2020.

4. Reassessment of the WBST priorities of the GSE in 2021
At its 14th emergency meeting in Paris on 2nd November 2020, The World Heritage
Committee decided that its 44th extended meeting would take place in June/July 2021, in
Fuzhou, in Fujian province, China. The 44th WHC meeting will be the only one in 2021. For
the GSE, this implies that the applications scheduled for discussion in July 2020 are being
moved for review by the midst of 2021.
The GSE nomination assessment materials will be received by the States Parties to the GSE
serial nomination six weeks before the UNESCO WHC meeting commencement. For the
WBST, this represents an opportunity to reassess priorities for the period 2020-2021, with a
focus on supporting activities in the following four areas.
4.1 Protection: Focus on care for the protection and preservation of the nominated properties
which complies with the principles of the protection of the outstanding universal value (OUV)
of the property and which will enable sustainable development in the emergency mode of the
pandemic for the foreseeable future (on local and regional level).
4.2 Marketing: Focus on local tourism's target groups that understand the values of The
World Heritage sites and that do not threaten but help to protect and develop the economic
prosperity of our spas in the context of jointly coordinated marketing activities within the
context of the GSE. As a sample at the present time, through a jointly coordinated GSE
promotion, a mutually beneficial initiative already occurred, cf. spa cups initiative (on local,
regional and international level).
9

 4.3 Transport: Focus on finding balances among the city's public transport services by
optimising them with regard to residents, employees, and visitors. Transport is one of the key
tools for regulating tourism. We strive for the most optimal solutions and ways of spa town
transport services, but also for new ways of connecting with our neighbouring cities within
the Karlovy Vary Region, and with our closest neighbours abroad such as Bavaria, Saxony
and Austria (on local, regional, national and international level).
4.4 Development: Focus on new tourism marketing to become more oriented on new
circumstances in the spa town environment. We understand that the UNESCO WH listing is
likely to change the overall direction of our spa town's future. We need and want to be
prepared for expected changes so that we are in line with the proper vision on the level of
urban planning as well as strategic planning in the context of the GSE serial nomination in a
foreseeable future (on local, regional, national and international level).
Conclusion
The future prospects for the development of the nominated property, the component of
Mariánské Lázně, are now strongly influenced by the global crisis caused by the coronavirus
pandemic. Not only has this negatively affected the normal operation of spa towns across
Europe, but it has also radically changed our priorities in planning for the next steps following
the emergence of the crisis regime, which forces the whole country and all local authorities to
operate under emergency conditions, such as repeatedly prolonged states of emergency
lockdowns. The current shifts in priorities reflect the emphasis on new modes of marketing,
the reorientation of the marketing strategy and the development on novel concepts of tourism
and destination management with a view to global restrictions on tourism, as can also be seen
at the actions of the European Tourism Alliance, which calls on EU Member States to
harmonise their actions in the tourism sector to help the travel industry to survive this
unprecedented crisis.(cf. for example to the priorities of The European Tourist Manifesto
issued on 20 May 2020 in Brussels).
At the municipal level, the shift is in emphasis on public transport infrastructure, which
remains at stake, including parking solutions for tourist transport in the designated areas.
Future projects must perceive some trends aimed at overcoming the consequences of the
economic crisis caused by nationwide lockdowns in the Czech Republic and elsewhere in the
world, but especially in the neighbouring countries of our region in the Czech Republic
(Saxony, Bavaria, Austria etc.). The preparation for implementing a new urban conservation
area regeneration programme is being placed on hold and postponed by a year. Protection and
maintenance planning, i.e. the plan for the protection and preservation of the principal
elements with the OUV in the center of the spa town protected zone remain unaffected and
unchanged.
